title: Runbook metadata enrichment and idempotent executor
creator: Liam Chen
description: Add structured metadata to existing runbook step definitions and build an idempotent executor service that can safely replay, resume, and partial-apply runbooks for oncall/support workflows. This ticket covers: 1) schema for runbook step metadata (tags, side-effects, read/write resources, idempotency token rules, safety gates); 2) a small shim service (runbook-exec) that enforces idempotency, persists step outputs, and exposes a dry-run / resume API; 3) migration plan and fast path for converting top-priority runbooks; 4) telemetry and tracing for step-level latency, failure modes, and cost impact. Goal is to reduce human error during remediation, make dry-runs reliable for playbooks, and enable partial automation for high-frequency fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook step schema PR merged and documented in Confluence with examples and a backwards-compatibility section
runbook-exec service implements per-step idempotency token semantics and persists outputs to the runbook store; verified by unit + integration tests
Canary: migrate 3 low-risk runbooks (billing-retry, disk-cleanup, log-rotate) to new schema and exercise resume/dry-run paths without customer-visible impact
Grafana dashboard shows step-level success/failure rates, average resume time, and dry-run vs live divergence metric
Playbook replays produce deterministic outputs for idempotent steps and are blocked by safety gates when a non-idempotent change is attempted
